s0
{शिव} never destroyed anything.
Shiva never destroyed anything.
s1
And before you get angry... try destroying something yourself.
And before you get angry… try destroying something yourself.
s2
Burn a piece of wood. It turns into ash, smoke, heat, and light.
Burn a piece of wood. It turns into ash, smoke, heat and light.
s3
Count the atoms. Not a single one is lost.
Count the atoms. Not a single one is lost.
s4
Ice melts. Water rises. Clouds come back as rain.
Ice melts. Water rises. Clouds come back as rain.
s5
Forms end. Nothing ends.
Forms end. Nothing ends.
s6
So what does {शिव} destroy?
So what does Shiva destroy?
s7
Take a clay pot. There's space inside it. Its own little space.
Take a clay pot. There's space inside it. Its own little space.
s8
Now, break the pot.
Now… break the pot.
s9
Did that space die? It was never separate from the sky.
Did that space die? It was never separate from the sky.
{गौडपाद} said this, over a thousand years ago.
Gauḍapāda said this, over a thousand years ago.
When the pot breaks, its space merges back into space. So does every me, into the Self.
When the pot breaks, its space merges back into space. So does every “me”… into the Self.
That's what {शिव} destroys. Not the world. The walls.
That's what Shiva destroys. Not the world. The walls.
The wall that says, this is me, and that's everything else.
The wall that says, “this is me… and that's everything else.”
The {शिव} {सूत्र} begin with two words. {चैतन्यम् आत्मा}. Consciousness is the Self.
The Śiva Sūtras begin with two words. Caitanyam ātmā. Consciousness is the Self.
The awareness reading these words, right now, was never inside a pot.
The awareness reading these words right now… was never inside a pot.
And {शंकर} sang it plainly. {शिवोऽहम्}. I am {शिव}.
And Śaṅkara sang it plainly. Śivo'ham. I am Shiva.
Not a god far away. The sky you always were.
Not a god far away. The sky you always were.
That's {सनातन}. Break your pot, on living {सनातन} dot com.
That's Sanātan. Break your pot — on livingsanatan.com
